0|2e9bd483159939ed2c0704b914294653c8341d25|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"mm: memcg/slab: pre-allocate obj_cgroups for slab caches with SLAB_ACCOUNT
In general it's unknown in advance if a slab page will contain accounted
objects or not.  In order to avoid memory waste
allocated dynamically when a need to account of a new object arises.  Such
approach is memory efficient
column2: but requires an expensive cmpxchg() to set

column1: up the memcg/objcgs pointer
column2: because an allocation can race with a

column1: different allocation on another cpu.
But in some common cases it's known for sure that a slab page will contain
accounted objects: if the page belongs to a slab cache with a SLAB_ACCOUNT
flag set.  It includes such popular objects like vm_area_struct
task_struct
In such cases we can pre-allocate the objcgs vector and simple assign it
to the page without any atomic operations
column2: because at this early stage the

column1: page is not visible to anyone else.
A very simplistic benchmark (allocating 10000000 64-bytes objects in a
row) shows ~15% win.  In the real life it seems that most workloads are
not very sensitive to the speed of (accounted) slab allocations.
